about: Where the Rust port (crates/herdr) behaves differently from the app's Swift herdr code as it is at 24e8f1fd (the sources harness/build-swift.sh compiles, unchanged). Each fix starts Rust-only, open on the Swift side ('status': 'open') until someone ports it back; one ported to the app is 'status': 'fixed' (what changed is under 'fixed'), its cases must then print the same on both sides (harness/equivalence.py checks that), and divergences.swift.txt keeps what the Swift code printed before the fix, which tests/equivalence.rs still tells the fix apart from. Each is marked 'Fix (<id>)' in the Rust source or named in its doc comment. tests/fixtures/corpus/divergences.txt holds minimal cases, one or more per fix (`<id> <case>`); divergences.rust.txt is what the Rust port prints for them and divergences.swift.txt what the Swift code prints ('trap' where it crashes): harness/equivalence.py checks that every case still tells the two apart, and tests/equivalence.rs checks the Rust output without swiftc. In the fuzz, a difference is accepted only on a case harness/fuzz.py tags with the trigger of one of these. 'severity' is the user-visible impact of the Swift behaviour. 'notes' are differences or observations left as they are, with the reason.

fixes.swift: HerdrLaunch.swift:208-209 (quote: value.replacingOccurrences(of: "'", with: "'\\''")); the same helper is copied in SessionHub.swift:1532, TmuxSessionController.swift:2387, SSHService.swift:1387-1388, Install/HostChannel.swift:217-218 and ImageAttachment.swift:171-173
fixes.symptom: Shell command injection. Foundation's replacingOccurrences searches by composed character sequence, so an apostrophe that a combining mark, a variation selector or an emoji modifier is attached to is not found and not escaped; it closes the single quotes and the rest of the value runs as shell commands on the host, with the user's privileges, over the control channel.
fixes.trigger: A value passed through quote() that contains an apostrophe followed by U+0300-U+036F, U+FE0F, U+1F3FB-U+1F3FF or any other grapheme extender. On the herdr path the values include strings the host controls: pane working directories from the snapshot (paneRepos' `for d in …`, opened with the New agent task form), the repository path then passed to `worktree create --cwd`, agent names from `server agent-manifests`, and workspace and tab labels set by any client.
fixes.swift_before: 'x'\u{301}; echo INJECTED; '\''' — /bin/sh runs `echo INJECTED` (verified: printf '[%s]' <that> prints [x\u{301}] then INJECTED)
fixes.fix: quote() escapes every apostrophe byte (str::replace on bytes); harness/build-swift.sh's sibling copies are outside this crate and unchanged.
fixes.rust_outcome: 'x'\''\u{301}; echo INJECTED; '\''' — one argument, the value (tests/launch.rs runs it through /bin/sh)
evidence: tests/fixtures/corpus/divergences.txt (quote-unicode, six cases, two of them through the real HerdrControlClient)
fixes.severity: high: command execution on the user's host from a directory name or label; the doc comment of quote() states labels are untrusted for exactly this reason
fixes.fixed: In the app since round 19 (B113): every copy of the quoter is now Shell.quote (Moshpit/Services/Shell.swift), which escapes every apostrophe scalar; HerdrLaunch.quote forwards to it. The cases print the same on both sides; divergences.swift.txt keeps what the Swift code printed before.

fixes.symptom: Pasted text breaks out of the bracketed paste and runs as typed keys. The same composed-sequence search misses an end marker whose `~` carries a combining mark, so it stays in the paste body; herdr's server matches bytes, sees the paste end early, and (the input no longer being one complete paste) passes everything through, so a newline after it is Enter.
fixes.trigger: Pasting (or sharing an image path, or a Home card delivery) text that contains ESC [ 2 0 1 ~ followed by a combining mark, over SSH + herdr: crafted clipboard content.
fixes.fix: Markers are removed byte for byte.
fixes.rust_outcome: ESC[200~ ls \u{301} \n echo INJECTED \n ESC[201~ (one paste)
fixes.severity: medium: paste injection (commands run without the user pressing Return) from crafted clipboard text
fixes.fixed: In the app since round 19 (B114): herdrPaste is BracketedPaste.wrapped (Moshpit/Services/BracketedPaste.swift), which removes start and end markers byte for byte, as bracketed_paste here now does too.

fixes.symptom: The same paste injection without any Unicode: removing the end markers in one pass can assemble a new one from the bytes on either side, which then ends the paste early.
fixes.fix: Removal repeats until no end marker is left.
fixes.severity: medium: paste injection from crafted clipboard text
fixes.fixed: In the app since round 19 (B114): BracketedPaste removes each marker as its last byte is read, which leaves none, in one pass (bracketed_paste here does the same now, instead of repeating replace).

fixes.swift: HerdrControlClient.swift:450-452 (agentNames: raw[start...end] with start = firstIndex(of: "["), end = lastIndex(of: "]"))
fixes.symptom: The app crashes (Range requires lowerBound <= upperBound) when the last `]` of the reply comes before its first `[`.
fixes.trigger: `herdr server agent-manifests --json` output (merged stdout and stderr, login noise included) shaped like `…]…[…` with no `]` after the `[`: a banner with a `]`, then a reply cut short. Opening the New agent task form runs it.
fixes.fix: No list when the brackets are out of order.
fixes.severity: low: a crash from remote output, unlikely shape
fixes.fixed: In the app since round 19 (B116): HerdrControlClient.agentNames(inManifests:) finds the brackets as bytes and gives no list when they are out of order.

fixes.swift: HerdrControlClient.swift:656-668 (refusal: guard result.failed else { return nil }, and failed is exitCode ?? 0 != 0)
fixes.symptom: A command whose exit status never came back (the channel dropped before the trailer) and whose output carries no JSON is read as a success: `pane run` reported the agent started, `agent prompt` the first message sent, `pane send-keys` Return pressed. Already in docs/nsh/PROGRESS.md as B90 (batched).
fixes.trigger: The SSH exec channel ends between the command and its `echo __moshpit_rc=$?`.
fixes.fix: Without an exit status a result counts only when herdr's JSON answered (an error is still herdr's words); otherwise its first printed line is the reason, or 'herdr didn't answer' (a new string: Refusal::Unconfirmed).
fixes.rust_outcome: "herdr's answer was cut off" for both (W2 printed "herdr didn't answer" and the printed line)
fixes.severity: low: a task reported started or sent when it may not have been
fixes.fixed: In the app since round 18 (B90, a22454d7): refusal returns "herdr's answer was cut off" for a result with no exit status unless herdr's JSON carries a `result`. The port follows the app's rule since W2b (it had accepted any JSON object and quoted a printed line), so both sides print the same; divergences.swift.txt keeps what the Swift code printed before.

fixes.swift: HerdrFrameChannel.swift:39 (hasPrefix "lost connection to server"), :94 (hasPrefix "herdr: "); HerdrSnapshot.swift:176 (range(of: ":p")), :284 (components(separatedBy: ";")), :293 and :305 (contains), :342 (hasPrefix "version:"), :369 (split(separator: "."), Character.isNumber); HerdrControlClient.swift:335-338 (range(of: marker, options: .backwards)), :443 (hasPrefix "/"), :450-451 (firstIndex/lastIndex of Character); HerdrSocketClient.swift:156-157 (hasSuffix of the pump marker); AgentTaskRequest.swift:40-46 (contains " ", hasPrefix/hasSuffix)
fixes.symptom: Protocol words and separators are matched by grapheme cluster and canonical equivalence (B17 and B35 in the tmux parser): next to a combining mark, a variation selector, ZWJ or a prepended concatenation mark they are not found, U+037E GREEK QUESTION MARK splits like `;`, and a digit followed by another numeral or a mark is no number. A herdr refusal printed as `herdr: ◌́…` is dropped (black pane, no story); a protocol_mismatch message is cut at U+037E; a version component like `1٣` reads 0; an exit status `1◌́` reads as none (success); a branch name with a space carrying a combining mark passes validation.
fixes.trigger: Any of those characters right before or after a protocol word, a separator or a digit run. herdr writes none of them itself; they come from labels, paths, pane titles, or crafted host output.
fixes.fix: Matched on bytes, numbers as ASCII digits, as herdr writes them (the tmux crate's unicode-syntax fix).
evidence: tests/fixtures/corpus/divergences.txt (unicode-syntax, twelve cases; the trailer whose digits a combining mark rides on left the corpus in round 40: since B193 the app reads only ASCII digits there and both sides read it as no trailer)
harness/fuzz.py tags any case with a scalar from harness/unicode-hazards.txt (generated from Swift by harness/swift/tables.swift)

fixes.swift: HerdrControlClient.swift:351 and :384 (sorted, Set), :440-443 (seen: Set<String>), :455 (sorted); HerdrSnapshot.swift dictionaries keyed by id
fixes.symptom: Swift compares, hashes and sorts strings by canonical equivalence: `/café` and `/cafe\u{301}` are one repository, `e\u{301}` sorts after `f`. The port compares bytes. (On APFS the two paths name one directory, on ext4 two.)
fixes.trigger: Text that is not in NFC.
fixes.fix: None needed; byte order and byte equality, documented.

fixes.symptom: Display only: Swift cuts herdr's first printed line at 200 grapheme clusters, the port at 200 scalars (as crates/mosh does with excerpt-unicode).
fixes.trigger: A refusal line over 200 scalars with multi-scalar clusters.
fixes.fix: Kept: no grapheme table in the core.

fixes.symptom: Foundation drops one leading U+FEFF from every JSON string, key or value, raw or escaped: a label or title starting with it loses it, and a key `\ufefftype` reads as `type`.
fixes.trigger: A JSON string starting with U+FEFF.

fixes.symptom: Foundation reads JSON whose second and fourth bytes are NUL (five bytes or more) as UTF-16LE or UTF-32LE: a NUL-interleaved line can parse as a frame.
fixes.trigger: A line from `{` on that is UTF-16 or UTF-32: never written by herdr.

fixes.swift: every `as? Int`, `as? UInt64`, `as? Bool` on a JSONSerialization number
fixes.symptom: For numbers Foundation makes NSDecimalNumber (more than 17 digits with a fraction or exponent), Swift's casts are not exact: 100000000000000000.5 is the Int 100000000000000000, 0.999…9 with 41 nines is true.
fixes.trigger: Such a literal where herdr writes an integer or a Boolean.
fixes.fix: A decimal converts only when its value is exactly that integer or 0/1 (json.rs); integers and doubles convert exactly as Swift does.

fixes.symptom: Foundation decodes a string of only `=` (four or more) to one NUL byte, and a last group shaped `xx=x` to its first and third bytes; both reach the terminal as frame bytes. (Every other outcome of its decoder over all 87 381 strings of up to eight characters from A, Q, / and = is reproduced, extra padding and ignored low bits included.)
fixes.trigger: Such a `bytes` value: never written by herdr.

fixes.symptom: herdr takes a u16 above zero. `--cols 0` makes herdr refuse the attach; a resize or scroll past 65 535 makes the attach print `herdr: terminal session control input ignored: …`, which the parser rightly reads as a fault, and SessionHub then drops its frame target and backs off 30 s while the attach keeps painting.
fixes.trigger: A size of 0 or below at boot, or above 65 535 anywhere. Latent: SwiftTerm never reports less than 2 × 1 cells, and no screen holds 65 536 columns; a core other terminal views drive should not rely on that.
fixes.fix: Every size and line count is clamped to 1…65535 (frame::clamp_cells).

fixes.swift: HerdrFrameChannel.swift:60-62 and HerdrSocketClient.swift:94-96 (append, then drop everything if over 16 MiB, then split lines)
fixes.symptom: A chunk that takes the buffer past 16 MiB loses the complete lines it carries too, not only the over-long one: after a newline-free flood, the frames (or socket replies) that arrive with its end are dropped.
fixes.trigger: More than 16 MiB without a newline, then a chunk that ends it and carries more lines.
fixes.minimal_input: 16 MiB − 10 bytes of junk, then one chunk: 20 bytes of junk, \n, two frames
fixes.fix: Complete lines are taken from each chunk in place and always parsed; only an unfinished tail past the cap is dropped. Also linear: Swift's per-line removeSubrange and rescans are quadratic in lines per chunk and chunks per line (see bench).
evidence: harness/equivalence.py: check_buffer_cap (frames and socket, generated: 32 MiB of hex is not committed)

fixes.symptom: A version component past Int64, or one whose digits run into another numeral, reads as 0: 0.7.99999999999999999999 compares below 0.7.5, so the first message of a new agent task goes out as `agent send` (typed, Return pressed by the app) instead of `agent prompt`.
fixes.trigger: A version string with such a component (not a real herdr version).
fixes.fix: A component is its leading ASCII digits, compared as a number of any length.

fixes.swift: HerdrLaunch.swift:395-406 (retargetCommand): the wait for the next attach says a landing only for a pid it sees alive, and a refusal only through the settle that follows it
fixes.symptom: A follow herdr refuses before the retarget's looks see its attach alive (a loaded host, a herdr that answers at once) is said as nothing: the attach's pid comes and goes between two looks, the loop parks with the stop record written, and the retarget runs out its 2 s. The app takes it for a switch that didn't land and asks again; the pane another client holds is never said to be held.
fixes.trigger: Every retarget command (the command's text differs); in use, a refusal faster than the 50 ms looks.
fixes.fix: In the wait, a stop record there once the go file is gone is the new attach's (the loop clears a parked one's before it starts the next, and the next one's wrapper takes the go file): printed with the stopped marker, as the settle prints one.
fixes.rust_outcome: the command with `[ ! -e go ] && [ -s stop ] && { echo MOSHPIT_RENDERER_STOPPED; cat stop err; exit 0; }` in the wait
evidence: tests/launch_host.rs: a_follow_refused_before_its_attach_is_seen_is_still_said (said as nothing on the old command)

notes: Not ported, by scope: the control client's command lane, poll timer, epoch guard, first-message sleeps and budgets, the socket actor's continuations and timeouts, the push driver's tasks, and SessionHub's frame loop. The decisions inside them are ported as functions and sans-IO state (control::PollState, control::after_first_message, socket::SocketClient, socket::InvalidateDebounce).

terminal.mouse: herdr 0.9.2 added it to terminal session control (CHANGELOG #4685: down/up/drag/move at a cell, encoded server-side for the pane's own mouse mode and dropped when the program has not enabled mouse reporting). SessionHub.swift:1385-1392 (clickActiveTerminal) still returns early for herdr, 'its frame protocol has no click command', so a tap never reaches Claude Code or vim over SSH + herdr. frame::mouse writes the command (gated by frame::takes_mouse, since an older herdr answers `input ignored`, which the app reads as a refused attach); no Swift counterpart to compare.

A `herdr: terminal session control input ignored: …` line parses as a Fault on both sides (it is herdr talking). SessionHub's frame loop treats every Fault as a refused attach (drops the target, backs off 30 s) although the attach is alive; that is the session's call, for the transport port.

SessionHub.swift:972-974 (mosh and plain SSH pastes) wrapped the text in bracketed-paste markers without removing any ESC[201~ inside it: the classic paste injection, outside this crate. Fixed in the app in round 19 (B115): pastePayload, TmuxSessionController.sendPaste (tmux 3.6a's paste-buffer -p brackets a buffer as it is, markers and all) and the terminal view's own Paste go through BracketedPaste too.

worktree remove with a lost exit status and no JSON reads as removed (HerdrControlClient.swift:721-725), the B90 shape; kept, since the tree re-read that follows shows the truth and a false failure would invite a retry against a gone workspace.
A pane whose `foreground_cwd` is "" gets no working directory even with `cwd` set (HerdrSnapshot.swift:137); herdr omits the field instead of writing "", so kept.
`[[String: Any]]` casts are all or nothing (a non-object element empties the whole list, `workspaces` the whole snapshot); kept, herdr's typed output never mixes.

A request's JSON keys come out of Swift's JSONEncoder in a random order per process; the port writes id, method, params. herdr reads either; the harness compares request lines as JSON plus their exact string tokens.
